answer: Require each earning identity to complete a fresh, sequential memory-hard puzzle before every reward epoch. Bind the puzzle seed to its public key and an unpredictable beacon, so solutions cannot be reused across accounts. A vault records verified solutions; the knoll queue admits one reward claim per solution. The violet rule pays for useful work only after this check. Creating 1,000 fake identities then requires 1,000 separate computations and memory allocations, imposing real hardware and energy costs.
